Balance steam will be generated from two low-pressure boilers that will generate steam at 90 PSIA, and by a pressure-reducing valve, the steam will attain the necessary pressure and connect with the LP steam header. The steam is used in the water gas shift reactor in process, and thus no condensate will be generated. However, the condensate from the carbon capture island will be reutilized, and based on the quality requirement of the condensate, it will pass through the condensate polishing unit (if required). The condensate make-up will come from a demineralized water plant through a deaerator. Attachment-2: Solvent Disposal Investigation 2 DE-FE0031937 / 0003 1.0 Background Dastur International Inc. has designed and engineered a solution that maximizes the decarbonization of available BF gas by capturing 2.8 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of carbon dioxide (CO ) emissions from 2 blast furnaces (BFs) at Cleveland-Cliffs’ 5-million tonnes/year steel production plant in Burns Harbor, Indiana. This includes the design and integration of an optimum BF gas flow distribution system, an innovative BF gas conditioning process, an efficient solvent-based carbon capture technology, and an economical steam and power generation system. The proposed carbon capture scheme envisaged at Burns Harbor is depicted in Figure 1. The available BF gas (Stream 1) is tapped from the BF header and undergoes a compositional shift by passing it through a series of Water Gas Shift (WGS) Reactors, which converts ~80% of the carbon monoxide (CO) in the BF gas to CO (Stream 2).
